packageRules.description: Auto-merge low-risk updates once CI passes
Auto-merge devDependency minor bumps once CI passes

Auto-merge workflow action minor bumps once CI passes (#101). Each action is pinned by SHA with a # vX.Y.Z comment (setup-node since #81, checkout and setup-bun since #97), so a minor release arrives as a minor PR. Before #97, checkout and setup-bun floated on @vN tags that took each minor release at run time with no PR. The PR's own CI runs the new action before the merge.

Keep the engines.bun floor out of the top-level rangeStrategy bump. The exact Bun pin is the packageManager field in package.json (#96), which CI's setup-bun steps and railpack on Coolify both install; engines.bun only states the floor. Under bump, a dry run opens a renovate/bun-1.x PR that raises ">=1.1.0" to the newest Bun (#89). auto leaves a range the newest Bun already satisfies alone.

Propose a Bun release for the packageManager pin only once it is 14 days old (#96). Before the pin, railpack resolved engines.bun on Coolify through mise, whose minimum_release_age of 14d held each Bun release back from production for 14 days; mise does not apply that hold to an exact version. Without this rule, the patch automerge rule above would ship a new Bun to production as soon as its PR's CI passes.

Open no PR for .nvmrc (#81). It names only the Node major: CI's setup-node and railpack on Coolify each pick a release of that major on their own (setup-node takes a cached one before it downloads), so CI and production share the major, not always the patch. Renovate's node versioning reads "26" as the single version 26.0.0, so a dry run proposes 26.13.0 now and would open a PR for every Node release, each writing a full version that then pins one release. A new Node major arrives as the @types/node major PR instead: in that PR, set .nvmrc and flake.nix nodejs_<major> to the same major. tests/node-pins.test.ts (#95) fails that PR's CI until they do.

Hold typescript below 7 (#103). TypeScript 7.0 drops the TypeScript 6 compiler API from its root export: require("typescript") returns only version and versionMajorMinor, and its new API sits under typescript/unstable/*. typescript-eslint, svelte-check and SvelteKit call the TypeScript 6 API, so on PR #55 svelte-kit sync failed in bun run check and vite build. Lift this rule once npm view <pkg>@latest peerDependencies accepts ^7 for each of typescript-eslint, svelte-check and @sveltejs/kit. The name match is exact, so typescript-eslint and the @typescript-eslint/* and @typescript/* packages still update.
